#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Do not delete the victim if it just exits in WaitingPods. 

We do `deleting pods` to free resources.  But if a pod exists in WaitingPods, it actually does not scheduled. So we just need reject it to free the resources from `NodeInfo`.

It sounds to me that you prefer to prioritize waiting Pod over other assigned Pods. In that case, you may want to exclude waiting Pods in the earlier Filtering/Sorting Victims step, instead of simply disregard the deletion in PrepareCandidate(). 

In general, when Permit plugins work along with PostFilter (preemption), the logic could be complicated. There may not be a general preemption implementation (probably in the future we can exercise pluginArgs to provide different options). So for now the best bet is to implement your own PostFilter plugin.

>

There may not be a general preemption implementation (probably in the future we can exercise pluginArgs to provide different options). So for now the best bet is to implement your own PostFilter plugin.

Got it!

But for the default preemption plugin, we delete the victims to free resources. 

If pod has assigned, we should delete it.
If pod has not assigned, we just need reject it in WaitingPod because the pod just exists in the `NodeInfo` cache.

> > If pod has not assigned, we just need reject it in WaitingPod because the pod just exists in the `NodeInfo` cache.
> 
> Oh, your point was to verify if it's a waiting pod first, and then delete it? If so, then it makes sense to me.
> 
> ```go
> if waitingPod := fh.GetWaitingPod(victim.UID); waitingPod != nil {
>     // reject it
> } else {
>     // delete the victim
> }
> ```
> 
> Feel free to raise a PR.
> 
> /assign @cwdsuzhou

Yes, I will open a PR to do this
